dct_title_s: India Floods: Flood Proxy Map, May 2022
dct_description_sm: # EOS-RS Flood Proxy Map: India, Floods, 18 May 2022, v0.4 The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) created this preliminary Flood Proxy Map (FPM) depicting areas that are likely flooded in Assam, India due to heavy rains that started on 13 May 2022. This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the Copernicus Sentinel-1 satellites operated by the European Space Agency (ESA) before (6 May 2022) and during (18 May 2022) the event. The image covers an area indicated by the large white polygon. Each light blue pixel measures about 30 meters across. This map was validated using reports of flooded areas in New Haflong Railway Station and along the Kampur-Kathiatoli Road. This flood proxy map should be used as a guide to identify areas that are likely flooded, and is less reliable over urban and vegetated areas. The product contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2022), processed by ESA and analyzed by the Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS), using the Advanced Rapid Imaging and Analysis (ARIA) system originally developed at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology, and modified at EOS-RS. **More map details and files:** **More map details and files:**
